status: Authored; current validation status is in docs/t25-course/RUN-LOG.md. Not learner-piloted.

sources.historicalAudit: 2026-09-14 v2 classification metadata; not a newly certified solution key

targets.title: Preserve domains under rewriting
targets.exactScope: Preserve denominator, real-root and logarithm domains under rewriting. Include principal roots, absolute value, rational powers in reduced form, and real log-law hypotheses; a cancellation never restores an excluded point.
targets.exitCheck: Compare two algebraically equal expressions as functions. State when sqrt(u²)=u and when it is -u; justify a rational-power or log identity on its actual domain.
steps: Compare domains before and after one cancellation.
Justify principal-root, rational-power and log-law conditions on a new expression.

targets.title: Treat equations as solution sets
targets.exactScope: Separate equivalent steps from one-way implications. Check sign cases before multiplying inequalities; check candidates after squaring.
targets.exitCheck: Solve one rational inequality by sign intervals and reject one extraneous root introduced by squaring.
steps: Classify each step of one equation as equivalent or implication-only.
Solve one inequality by sign cases and check all boundary points.

targets.title: Changed inputs and parameters
targets.exactScope: Distinguish f(x+h), f(x)+h and f(x+h)-f(x). Track variable, parameter and constant; compose affine functions and identify the domain of a changed input.
targets.exitCheck: For a domain-restricted function, write the legal domain of f(ax+b) and explain how a parameter changes it.
steps: Track one changed input and its legal domain.
Analyse one parameter or affine-iteration question.

targets.title: Claims and counterexamples
targets.exactScope: Negate quantified statements correctly; distinguish necessary/sufficient conditions and examples from proof.
targets.exitCheck: Negate an all/exists statement, disprove a false converse, and write a short implication proof with its assumptions.
steps: Negate one quantified claim and test a converse.
Write one short proof or a decisive counterexample.

targets.title: Sets, relations and inverse functions
targets.exactScope: Use unions/intersections/complements and Cartesian products; test equivalence relations and injectivity/surjectivity on stated sets.
targets.exitCheck: Find equivalence classes in one finite example; decide whether a specified function has an inverse and on which domain.
steps: Translate set operations and images/preimages by membership.
Check a relation and list its equivalence classes.
Test injectivity/surjectivity and construct an inverse on stated sets.

targets.title: Polynomial factors, coefficients and roots
targets.exactScope: Use the remainder/factor theorem and Vieta relations; distinguish repeated roots and multiplicities.
targets.exitCheck: Infer a coefficient/root constraint and determine whether a repeated root is possible without guessing from a graph.
steps: Use factor/remainder and Vieta in one root-coefficient problem.
Test a polynomial identity or repeated-root condition using degree and roots.

targets.title: Finite sums and progressions
targets.exactScope: Derive AP/GP sums with indexing and ratio-one exceptions; translate HP through reciprocals; handle simple geometric tails.
targets.exitCheck: Reindex a finite sum, evaluate a weighted geometric sum and state the condition for an infinite GP to converge.
steps: Derive an indexed AP/GP/HP relation with exceptional cases.
Evaluate a weighted geometric or telescoping sum, with its convergence condition.

targets.title: Inequalities, means and equality cases
targets.exactScope: Use AM-GM-HM for positive inputs, finite Cauchy-Schwarz and elementary convexity/Jensen when its definition is supplied. State equality cases; root counts needing derivatives belong to C4.
targets.exitCheck: Prove one sharp bound, identify every equality case, and give a counterexample after removing a necessary sign condition.
steps: Prove one AM-GM-HM or Cauchy-Schwarz bound with equality conditions.
Use a supplied convexity definition in one inequality or counterexample.

targets.title: Sequences, subsequences and functional constraints
targets.exactScope: Work with the definition of sequence convergence, monotonicity, boundedness, subsequences, recurrence and elementary squeeze arguments. Use composition/periodicity to test functional claims; no abstract real-analysis machinery.
targets.exitCheck: Construct a bounded nonconvergent sequence; prove a monotone bounded example converges. Explain why two different subsequential limits prevent convergence.
steps: Decide monotonicity/boundedness and construct a counterexample.
Prove one sequence/subsequence or recurrence limit.
Test one composition or periodicity constraint.

targets.title: Unit circle and trigonometric equations
targets.exactScope: Use radians, signs, basic identities and angle addition; solve equations with full periodic families and legal domains.
targets.exitCheck: Simplify a root/trigonometric expression with correct absolute values and solve one equation on a specified interval.
steps: Establish signs, radians, basic identities and sine/cosine rules.
Solve one periodic equation or triangle-identity task with domain checks.

targets.title: Complex arithmetic and polar form
targets.exactScope: Use conjugates, modulus and argument; apply De Moivre with all root branches and the z=0 exception.
targets.exitCheck: Solve a roots-of-unity or conjugate equation and explain whether its solution set is finite or a locus.
steps: Translate between Cartesian and polar complex form.
Solve one root-of-unity or conjugate-locus question with every branch.

targets.title: Lines, circles and intersections
targets.exactScope: Translate slopes, distances and tangency into equations; complete the square and retain degeneracy cases.
targets.exitCheck: Find a line through two circle centres and determine a tangent/intersection condition without an unjustified diagram assumption.
steps: Turn a line/circle/distance problem into equations.
Check tangency, reflection, intersections or a rational-point construction.

targets.title: Ordered versus unordered experiments
targets.exactScope: Specify outcomes, replacement and equiprobability; derive product/permutation/combination counts from choices.
targets.exitCheck: Count the same selection with and without order and explain the conversion factor instead of quoting it blindly.
steps: Specify ordered elementary outcomes and whether they are equiprobable.
Derive the correct permutation/combination count for that model.

targets.title: Counts with restrictions
targets.exactScope: Count restrictions by disjoint cases, complements, bijections and symmetry correction. Derive binomial and multinomial expansions by counting assignments to factors; use their coefficients and identities without double counting.
targets.exitCheck: Count constrained functions or pairings in two valid ways; identify why an attractive factorial count overcounts.
steps: Count one restricted arrangement using cases, gaps or a bijection.
Handle one symmetry/overcounting, parity or binomial/multinomial-coefficient problem.

targets.title: Event arithmetic on nonuniform spaces
targets.exactScope: Use nonnegativity, normalisation, complements, finite inclusion-exclusion and the union bound. State countable additivity and probability continuity for increasing/decreasing events; use these only to pass a justified finite calculation to a limit.
targets.exitCheck: Check a nonuniform assignment for coherence, calculate an overlapping union, and obtain an infinite-union probability as a limit of finite unions.
steps: Derive and use complement, inclusion-exclusion and union bounds.
Pass a finite event calculation to a monotone limit with the stated probability law.

targets.title: Conditioning, partitions and Bayes
targets.exactScope: Rebuild the conditioned reference class; derive multiplication, total probability and Bayes from event masses. Keep the conditioning probability positive and track information revealed by sampling.
targets.exitCheck: Solve a reverse-conditioning problem from a table or tree and explain exactly which denominator changes.
steps: Compute a conditional law directly from event masses.
Reverse the information direction using a partition and Bayes.

targets.title: Independence and conditional changes
targets.exactScope: Check event factorisation while keeping set-theoretic disjointness A∩B=∅ distinct from merely having P(A∩B)=0, including zero-probability edge cases. Separate pairwise from mutual independence and independence after conditioning. Extend finite products to infinite independent unions using P3.
targets.exitCheck: Determine disjointness and independence separately in an explicitly specified model that includes a zero-probability edge case; construct pairwise independent events that are not mutually independent; show how conditioning can destroy independence.
steps: Test independence and contrast it with disjointness.
Separate pairwise, mutual and conditional independence in one counterexample.

targets.title: Expectation through indicators
targets.exactScope: Treat a finite payoff as a random variable; express a count as a sum of indicators; use linearity without assuming independence.
targets.exitCheck: Find an expected count when events overlap; state which parts need independence and which do not.
steps: Encode a payoff or count as a random variable or sum of indicators.
Derive its expectation without adding an unnecessary independence assumption.

targets.title: Variance, covariance and dependent sums
targets.exactScope: Derive Var(X)=E(X²)-E(X)² and covariance bilinearity when moments exist. Expand variance of dependent sums; identify which cross terms vanish. For continuous examples, return after D3/J3.
targets.exitCheck: Derive the variance of a finite dependent sum; for a recurrence with independent innovations, propagate a variance and a lag covariance correctly.
steps: Derive variance/covariance identities and a finite dependent-sum calculation.
Propagate moments through an overlapping sum or linear recurrence.

targets.title: Bernoulli, binomial, hypergeometric and multinomial
targets.exactScope: Write support and probability law; derive means/variances using indicators; distinguish with/without replacement.
targets.exitCheck: Choose the correct law from a sampling story and calculate one marginal/count probability without confusing trials and categories.
steps: Derive binomial and hypergeometric probabilities from the experiment.
Obtain multinomial means, variances, covariances and one conditional count law.

targets.title: Geometric, negative binomial and Poisson
targets.exactScope: Declare whether waiting counts trials or failures; use series and independence to derive elementary moments and sums.
targets.exitCheck: Derive one geometric waiting law with its convention and one Poisson factorial moment; recognise binomial-to-Poisson approximation conditions.
steps: Derive a waiting-time law with an explicit trials/failures convention.
Use Poisson sums/factorial moments or a justified binomial approximation.

targets.title: Sampling means and sample variance
targets.exactScope: Derive the mean and variance of a sample average and unbiasedness of the n-1 sample variance under iid sampling with finite variance; normality is unnecessary here. Distinguish centred and uncentred mean squares.
targets.exitCheck: Prove unbiasedness of the n−1 variance estimator and identify the hidden cross terms in a non-iid alternative.
steps: Derive the variance of a sample average.
Derive the n-1 variance correction without assuming normality.

targets.title: Descriptive measures and data updates
targets.exactScope: Compute mean, median, quantiles/IQR, raw/central moments, sample/population variance, skewness and kurtosis under declared conventions. Track how sums and squared sums change when observations are added; define coefficient of variation only where meaningful.
targets.exitCheck: Update a mean and variance after adding one observation; explain a quantile/tie convention and distinguish raw kurtosis from excess kurtosis.
steps: Compute descriptive summaries with explicit denominator and quantile conventions.
Update sums/squared sums and explain a scale, skewness or kurtosis measure.

targets.title: Pearson, Spearman and regression-line identities
targets.exactScope: Compute Pearson correlation and Spearman as Pearson correlation of ranks, with a stated tie rule. Relate the two simple-regression slopes and R² to correlation; distinguish linear from monotone association, and within-group from pooled correlation.
targets.exitCheck: Build an uncorrelated dependent example and a perfectly ranked but nonlinear example; state when correlation is undefined and why pooling groups can reverse a sign.
steps: Compute Pearson and Spearman and state their existence/tie conditions.
Use regression-line identities or construct a pooling/nonlinearity counterexample.

targets.title: Matrix arithmetic and row operations
targets.exactScope: Multiply conformable matrices, transpose products, and perform reversible elementary row operations. Distinguish entrywise powers from matrix powers and AB from BA.
targets.exitCheck: Row-reduce a small augmented matrix, recording valid operations; give one concrete example where AB differs from BA.
steps: Multiply and transpose conformable matrices correctly.
Perform reversible row operations on one small system.

targets.title: Span, independence and basis
targets.exactScope: Check subspaces; exhibit a dependence or prove independence; find a basis and dimension by elimination.
targets.exitCheck: Find a basis for a small constrained vector or polynomial space and justify the dimension, including exceptional parameter values.
steps: Test a proposed subspace and a dependence relation.
Find and justify a basis/dimension for a constrained space.

targets.title: Rank and solution existence
targets.exactScope: Row-reduce Ax=b; compare coefficient and augmented ranks; describe null space and all solutions.
targets.exitCheck: Give exact parameter cases for no solution, one solution or infinitely many solutions; justify uniqueness using the null space.
steps: Classify consistency and solution dimension by ranks.
Prove a parameter-dependent uniqueness or rank-bound claim.

targets.title: Determinant and invertibility structure
targets.exactScope: Use determinant row operations, products, triangular structure and recurrences; relate determinant, inverse and rank.
targets.exitCheck: Derive a small tridiagonal determinant recurrence; use it to decide singularity without a giant expansion.
steps: Use determinant/inverse/trace identities with order preserved.
Derive a structured determinant recurrence or singularity criterion.

targets.title: Eigenvalues, eigenspaces and matrix powers
targets.exactScope: Use characteristic polynomials, trace/determinant and conjugate roots for real matrices. Distinguish algebraic/geometric multiplicity. Use diagonalisation or a supplied polynomial identity to compute matrix powers and construct square roots.
targets.exitCheck: Decide diagonalizability; construct square roots under stated spectral hypotheses. Distinguish at least a specified number from exactly that number.
steps: Find eigenspaces and determine whether diagonalisation is legal.
Use a polynomial identity or diagonalisation to obtain powers/roots.

targets.title: Symmetry, orthogonality and quadratic forms
targets.exactScope: Use real symmetric diagonalisation, orthogonal projection and positive semidefinite quadratic forms. Recognise xᵀAᵀAx as a squared length. Verify a proposed generalised-inverse identity directly when requested.
targets.exitCheck: Prove AᵀA is positive semidefinite and identify when it is positive definite; justify a projection or full-column-rank uniqueness claim.
steps: Relate a symmetric quadratic form to its spectrum.
Verify a projection, squared-length or generalised-inverse identity.

targets.title: Limits and continuity at difficult points
targets.exactScope: Compute one-sided limits using algebra, bounds and sequences; check continuity of piecewise and rational/irrational definitions.
targets.exitCheck: Decide continuity at a join and disprove an alleged limit using two approaching sequences.
steps: Evaluate a one-sided or piecewise limit with a stated definition.
Prove continuity or disprove a limit using two approaches.

targets.title: Derivative from the definition
targets.exactScope: Use the difference quotient and one-sided derivatives; separate continuity from differentiability.
targets.exitCheck: Derive the positive-integer power rule and test differentiability of an absolute-value/piecewise function at its join.
steps: Derive a polynomial sensitivity from the difference quotient.
Test differentiability at a join or oscillatory point.

targets.title: Differentiation rules with legal domains
targets.exactScope: Apply product, quotient and chain rules to polynomial, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic expressions.
targets.exitCheck: Differentiate a changed-input composite; identify every point where the displayed derivative formula is not justified.
steps: Establish/use product, quotient and chain rules on one composite.
Differentiate trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic expressions on their legal domains.

targets.title: Mean-value reasoning and root counts
targets.exactScope: Use IVT, Rolle and MVT with their exact hypotheses. Separate root existence from root uniqueness; handle fixed-point questions by elementary interval/sign arguments when possible.
targets.exitCheck: Prove a root exists and bound the number of roots; identify which conclusion fails on removing continuity or an endpoint condition.
steps: Prove existence via IVT and distinguish it from uniqueness.
Use Rolle/MVT for a root count, derivative bound or fixed-point argument.

targets.title: Optimisation and local approximation
targets.exactScope: Find constrained one-variable extrema; use a stated Taylor remainder or valid standard limit rather than an unsupported approximation.
targets.exitCheck: Compare a critical point with boundary values and justify one small-parameter limit with the order of the remainder.
steps: Optimise on the stated domain, comparing critical points and boundaries.
Justify one local approximation or limit with a valid Taylor remainder.

targets.title: Definite integrals, substitution and improper tails
targets.exactScope: Evaluate definite integrals using FTC, substitution, integration by parts, symmetry and interval splitting. Check endpoint and infinite-tail convergence before manipulating an improper integral.
targets.exitCheck: Evaluate one piecewise definite integral and determine the parameter range for convergence of one improper integral, with justification.
steps: Evaluate a definite integral by substitution, parts or interval splitting.
Determine the convergence range of one improper integral.

targets.title: Riemann sums and logarithms of products
targets.exactScope: Recognise a normalised finite sum as a Riemann sum. Turn a positive product/geometric mean into a sum of logarithms; justify endpoint treatment rather than applying a continuous-function rule blindly.
targets.exitCheck: Evaluate a sum-to-integral limit; explain what additional estimate is required when the integrand is unbounded at an endpoint.
steps: Recognise and justify a Riemann-sum limit.
Convert a positive product into a logarithmic sum and control a singular endpoint if present.

targets.title: Conic definitions and standard forms
targets.exactScope: Relate focus/directrix/eccentricity to standard parabola, ellipse and hyperbola equations.
targets.exitCheck: Classify a completed-square quadratic, including empty/point/pair-of-lines cases; locate focus/directrix for a nondegenerate example.
steps: Classify a completed-square quadratic, including degeneracy.
Recover focus/directrix/eccentricity for one standard conic.

targets.title: Conic parametrisation, tangents and normals
targets.exactScope: Use one suitable parametrisation per conic; derive tangent/normal conditions using differentiability or algebraic contact.
targets.exitCheck: Find a tangent at a parameter point and check vertical-tangent or undefined-slope exceptions.
steps: Use one conic parametrisation to locate a point.
Derive its tangent/normal and handle a vertical-slope exception.

targets.title: CDFs, supports, atoms and mixtures
targets.exactScope: Distinguish pmf, density and CDF. Check CDF monotonicity, right-continuity and limiting values; extract atoms from jumps and distinguish P(X<x) from P(X<=x). A continuous marginal need not imply a joint density.
targets.exitCheck: Accept or reject a proposed CDF with proof; build a distribution with both an atom and a continuous part, retaining both in probability calculations.
steps: Check CDF axioms and distinguish a jump from a density value.
Construct or characterise a mixed/atomic law from a CDF constraint.

targets.title: Uniform, exponential and normal
targets.exactScope: Use uniform, exponential and normal laws with their exact support/parameters; standardise normals and prove exponential memorylessness. Compute ordinary or tail-integral moments only when they exist.
targets.exitCheck: Compute probabilities and moments for each, and show precisely where memorylessness is used in a waiting-time argument.
steps: Work one uniform and one exponential probability/moment problem.
Standardise a normal probability and compute a required moment.

targets.title: Gamma, beta and moment transforms
targets.exactScope: Use gamma rate/scale, beta normalisation and gamma/chi-square connections. Derive moments and inverse-moment conditions; use MGF differentiation/product/uniqueness only on an open interval around zero where the MGF is finite. Recognise Poisson/binomial and common-rate gamma sum identities.
targets.exitCheck: Derive a gamma moment needed for an estimator and state when an inverse moment exists; combine independent gamma laws with a common rate.
steps: Use gamma/beta integrals and determine moment-existence ranges.
Identify a law or sum by an MGF with a valid existence domain.

targets.title: Univariate transformations
targets.exactScope: Use CDF events or branchwise density changes, retaining support and absolute derivative factors. Cover affine/square/absolute/exponential transforms and floor, ceiling or censoring; record any atoms.
targets.exitCheck: Derive the distribution after squaring or rounding a variable; check every inverse branch or jump and normalise the resulting law.
steps: Transform a continuous variable with every branch and correct support.
Derive a rounded, censored or mixed law from probability events.

targets.title: Distribution exceptions and supplied densities
targets.exactScope: Recognise Cauchy and Laplace distributions as compact extensions. Separate ordinary moments, absolute moments and principal values. For the standard Cauchy and declared p≥0, derive E|X|^p<∞ exactly for 0≤p<1 from tail behaviour; if a negative power is explicitly requested, also check local integrability near zeros rather than relying on tails alone. For an unfamiliar supplied density, derive support, normalisation and required moments instead of expanding a memorised catalogue.
targets.exitCheck: Show why the Cauchy mean is undefined despite symmetry; for declared p≥0 derive the exact absolute-moment range and explain what extra local check a negative exponent would require. For a Laplace density, compute a tail probability and identify its absolute-deviation structure.
steps: Check Cauchy moment/MGF existence, separating absolute moments.
Analyse the needed part of a Laplace or unfamiliar supplied density.

targets.title: Joint, marginal and conditional laws
targets.exactScope: For finite tables or plane regions, derive marginal and conditional laws, sketch support and integrate in the correct order. Conditional densities are used only where the marginal is positive. For Jacobians, establish the small partial-derivative/determinant toolkit in J5; do not assume a joint density always exists.
targets.exitCheck: Obtain both marginals and a conditional density from a triangular support and decide independence from the joint law.
steps: Recover joint/marginal laws from a finite table or planar support.
Compute a conditional law and check independence on the full support.

targets.title: Total expectation and total variance
targets.exactScope: Condition on a useful partition/random variable; separate within-condition variation from variation of conditional means.
targets.exitCheck: Calculate a mixture mean and variance in two ways and diagnose a missing variance component.
steps: Find an expectation by conditioning on useful information.
Derive total variance and apply it to a mixture or re-sampling scheme.

targets.title: Transformations of pairs and sums
targets.exactScope: Derive laws of sums, ratios and simple transformed pairs by CDF regions, convolution or invertible changes of variables. Establish the needed two-variable partial derivatives and absolute Jacobian determinant before using the formula; include all branches and transformed support.
targets.exitCheck: Find a transformed-pair or sum law, check its support and normalisation, and identify a shared-variable construction where a two-dimensional density does not exist.
steps: Find one sum/ratio law by regions or convolution.
Establish and use a two-variable Jacobian on an invertible branch.

targets.title: Squared and absolute loss; median logic
targets.exactScope: Minimise expected or sample squared/absolute deviation using finite sums, one-sided slopes or CDF probabilities. Means minimise squared loss under finite second moment; medians minimise absolute loss under finite first moment. Keep median intervals and weighted medians when minima are nonunique.
targets.exitCheck: Find all minimisers of a small absolute-deviation problem; explain the difference from least squares and handle a two-group regression or positive-input reciprocal transform.
steps: Compare minimisers of squared and absolute deviation.
Find all minimisers of one weighted, reciprocal-input or two-group absolute-loss problem.

targets.title: Stopping by first-step reasoning
targets.exactScope: Use geometric waiting times and elementary recurrences for finite-state or repeated independent trials; justify finite expectation when used.
targets.exitCheck: Compute a waiting-time expectation with an extra conditioning event. Do not import martingale/optional-stopping machinery for an elementary recurrence.
steps: Set up one first-step/waiting-time recurrence and its finite solution.
Solve one stopping question with additional conditioning or state information.

targets.title: Bivariate and multivariate normal
targets.exactScope: Use linear transformations of jointly normal vectors, covariance matrices and marginal/conditional formulas. Distinguish covariance from correlation; zero covariance implies independence only under joint normality. Handle singular perfect-correlation cases separately.
targets.exitCheck: Obtain a bivariate conditional mean/variance and decide when two linear forms of a normal vector are independent.
steps: Calculate covariance and independence of jointly normal linear forms.
Obtain a conditional normal law; handle a singular limit separately.

targets.title: Normal chi-square, t and F pivots
targets.exactScope: Obtain normal mean/residual independence from orthogonal normal coordinates. Build central chi-square, t and F laws with correct centring, scaling and independent numerator/denominator ingredients; do not confuse a bounded normal ratio with a t variable.
targets.exitCheck: Identify the distribution of a new ratio or show why it is not t/F when centring, denominator or independence is wrong.
steps: Establish normal mean/residual independence using orthogonal coordinates.
Assemble or reject one chi-square/t/F pivot with explicit degrees of freedom.

targets.title: Minima and maxima
targets.exactScope: Derive minimum/maximum laws from survival/CDF products. Distinguish iid from independent nonidentical samples and discrete from continuous extrema; use tail sums/integrals or direct moments.
targets.exitCheck: Find a shifted-exponential minimum law and its expectation; separately obtain a minimum of independent geometric variables with unequal parameters.
steps: Derive the CDF/survival of a minimum or maximum.
Compute an extreme moment or adapt the law to nonidentical/discrete samples.

targets.title: The kth order statistic
targets.exactScope: Express an order-statistic event as a binomial count; derive its continuous density under iid sampling.
targets.exitCheck: Derive the kth density with its combinatorial coefficient and check the minimum/maximum special cases.
steps: Translate a kth-order event into a binomial count.
Derive the continuous density and check its coefficient and endpoint cases.

targets.title: Joint order statistics, ranges and shared extrema
targets.exactScope: Derive/use the joint density of two order statistics under iid continuous sampling, then condition or obtain a range. Treat overlapping extrema built from shared observations separately: positive probability may be carried on the diagonal as a singular component even though no individual joint point is an atom.
targets.exitCheck: Obtain a conditional extreme or range law; for a shared-observation construction compute any positive equality probability and distinguish singular diagonal mass from a point atom.
steps: Obtain a joint order-statistic, conditional-extreme or range law.
Contrast it with shared-observation dependence carrying singular diagonal mass.

targets.title: Markov/Chebyshev as working bounds
targets.exactScope: State nonnegativity/finite-moment assumptions; obtain bounds for deviations and judge whether a bound is informative.
targets.exitCheck: Use Chebyshev to bound a sample-average error; explain why the bound is not an exact probability.
steps: Apply Markov/Chebyshev with all moment and sign conditions.
Judge whether the resulting bound is informative for a sample average.

targets.title: Weak law and consistency
targets.exactScope: Define convergence in probability and consistency. Apply an iid WLLN under finite absolute mean, or a vanishing-MSE/valid probability-bound argument where applicable. Track dependence explicitly. Asymptotic unbiasedness alone is insufficient, and nonvanishing bias or variance is not a general inconsistency converse without extra assumptions.
targets.exitCheck: For an estimator with overlapping or dependent terms, prove consistency with a valid probability-level argument or refute it by a fixed-epsilon nonvanishing error probability; do not infer inconsistency from moment nonconvergence alone.
steps: State WLLN and prove one iid-average consistency claim.
Prove or refute consistency when terms overlap or remain correlated.

targets.title: CLT standardisation and normal approximation
targets.exactScope: State/apply the iid finite-positive-variance CLT with correct centring and square-root scaling. Use independent blocks where justified, continuity correction for lattice probabilities, and elementary continuous-mapping/Slutsky statements for consistent plug-in terms; no general weak-convergence theory.
targets.exitCheck: Analyse a sum or difference of sums, identify its mean/variance and limiting law, and mark the approximation explicitly.
steps: Centre/scale a sum and calibrate a normal quantile.
Justify a block grouping or consistent plug-in approximation.

targets.title: Empirical counts and quantile consistency
targets.exactScope: Translate a kth-order event into an empirical count. Prove quantile concentration using WLLN with thresholds on either side of a uniquely identified quantile; state the required strict CDF inequalities.
targets.exitCheck: Prove a median/order-quantile concentration statement without memorising a density; distinguish a lower-tail result from full two-sided consistency.
steps: Express a quantile tail as an empirical-count event.
Use strict CDF inequalities and WLLN to prove the requested tail limit.

targets.title: Bias, variance and mean squared error
targets.exactScope: Compute bias, variance and MSE under the specified sampling law. Compare estimators over parameter/sample-size ranges, using factorial moments, transformed moments or dependent-sum expansions when appropriate.
targets.exitCheck: Compare two estimators by MSE and state for which parameter/sample-size values each is better.
steps: Compute bias, variance and MSE of one estimator.
Compare two candidates, preserving dependence and parameter ranges.

targets.title: Method of moments
targets.exactScope: Match theoretical to empirical moments within the admissible parameter space. Cover a one-parameter finite-population/count model and a two-parameter distribution; distinguish method of moments from MLE.
targets.exitCheck: Construct a two-parameter moment estimator and explain a sample for which the formal solution is inadmissible.
steps: Construct a one-parameter moment estimator.
Solve a two-moment or finite-population problem and check admissibility.

targets.title: Likelihood with parameter-dependent support
targets.exactScope: Write the likelihood for what was actually observed, including rounded/censored observations, support indicators and parameter constraints. Check interior optima, endpoints, disconnected feasible intervals and nonexistence. For transformed normal pairs, use the established J5 Jacobian and N3 normal-vector tools.
targets.exitCheck: Solve one smooth and one support-boundary likelihood problem; explain why rounding the MLE from unrounded data generally solves the wrong problem.
steps: Write and maximise one likelihood for the recorded observations.
Solve a boundary/disconnected-support likelihood and check whether a maximum exists.

targets.title: Invariance and constrained likelihood
targets.exactScope: Use MLE invariance for a parameter function; distinguish the model quantile from the sample quantile. For a small constrained normal likelihood, enforce equality and inequality constraints and check feasibility; do not launch a general optimisation course.
targets.exitCheck: Solve a small normal-mean estimation problem with a sum constraint and verify any inequality constraints separately.
steps: Find the MLE of a model probability, median or quantile by invariance.
Solve a small constrained normal-mean problem and check feasibility.

targets.title: Sufficient statistics
targets.exactScope: Apply factorisation including parameter-dependent support, or examine conditional laws given a statistic. Test sufficiency under a one-to-one recoding and under information loss; distinguish sufficiency, unbiasedness and consistency.
targets.exitCheck: Find a sufficient statistic in a one-parameter family and show why a plausible competing summary loses parameter information.
steps: Factor a likelihood with its support to establish sufficiency.
Test what happens when a sufficient statistic is recoded or coarsened.

targets.title: Variance improvement and minimum variance
targets.exactScope: Use Rao-Blackwell to improve an unbiased estimator. Distinguish improvement from a proof of minimum variance. Master two separate certificates: one complete-sufficiency/Lehmann-Scheffe argument and one attained Cramer-Rao bound in a regular standard model. State all hypotheses, the unbiased comparator class and why moving-support models can invalidate the routine information-bound route.
targets.exitCheck: Condition an unbiased estimator to improve it; then separately complete (i) a Lehmann-Scheffe UMVU certificate and (ii) an attained Cramer-Rao certificate in a regular model, plus diagnose one moving-support case where the latter is not licensed.
steps: Improve an unbiased estimator by conditioning on a sufficient statistic.
Certify minimum variance by completeness and by an information bound.

targets.title: Size, power, errors and p-values
targets.exactScope: Define simple/composite hypotheses, level, size, power, Type I/II error and p-value. Evaluate rejection probabilities under each law; use a union bound when several dependent rejection events are combined.
targets.exitCheck: For a discrete test compute actual size and power; explain why an unrandomised test may not attain an arbitrary nominal level exactly.
steps: Compute actual size, Type II error and power of a specified rule.
Distinguish a p-value from size and control a union of rejection events.

targets.title: Neyman–Pearson simple versus simple
targets.exactScope: Form the alternative/null likelihood ratio, choose the correct inequality, and calibrate its null probability.
targets.exitCheck: Derive a most-powerful rejection region and express its threshold using a known null distribution; explain if boundary randomisation is needed.
steps: Order observations by the alternative/null likelihood ratio.
Calibrate an exact MP rejection region, including randomisation if required.

targets.title: Normal-model tests
targets.exactScope: Choose z, t, chi-square or F from the stated known/unknown quantities and independence/normality assumptions.
targets.exitCheck: Construct one mean test and one variance test, checking degrees of freedom and tails. Do not infer a t law just from a ratio's appearance.
steps: Select and derive a normal mean or variance test.
Compare a two-sample test and its equivalent two-group ANOVA when assumptions match.

targets.title: Pivotal confidence intervals
targets.exactScope: Invert a genuine parameter-free pivot for a mean, variance, exponential mean or support endpoint. State exact versus approximate coverage, quantile-tail convention, and whether the target is a fixed parameter or a future observation.
targets.exitCheck: Derive a normal mean interval and a variance interval, then explain what their repeated-sampling coverage means.
steps: Invert a pivot with a declared quantile-tail convention.
Contrast parameter coverage with prediction or a one-sided bound.

targets.title: Approximate inference and transfer
targets.exactScope: Use standardisation/CLT and justified plug-in estimates; compare coverage/size approximations with exact alternatives.
targets.exitCheck: Build an asymptotic proportion interval or test and identify a small-sample/boundary regime where it is unreliable.
steps: Construct one CLT-based test or confidence interval.
State why a boundary, small sample or plug-in assumption can invalidate it.

targets.title: Sign and elementary count tests
targets.exactScope: Build a one-sample median or paired-difference sign test from independent Bernoulli signs under the null. State continuity/no-zero assumptions or the rule for ties; distinguish a paired median difference from equality of arbitrary population medians. Keep the scope to elementary exact count tests.
targets.exitCheck: Define the sign statistic, its null law and a rejection region; calculate actual size and explain what happens with ties or a different null probability.
steps: Specify the signs, null Bernoulli probability and treatment of zeros.
Calibrate an exact binomial sign-test rejection region.

targets.title: Least squares from minimisation
targets.exactScope: Derive normal equations with and without an intercept; use residual orthogonality and centred sums to prove coefficient identities and assess a changed observation or dummy variable. Identify zero denominators and nonidentifiability.
targets.exitCheck: Prove a coefficient identity from normal equations rather than fitting data numerically; state when the slope is identifiable.
steps: Derive simple-regression normal equations with/without intercept.
Prove a residual, dummy-variable or changed-observation identity.

targets.title: Multiple regression and covariance
targets.exactScope: Use fixed full-column-rank design matrices and projection. Derive coefficient bias/covariance under zero-mean homoskedastic uncorrelated errors without requiring normality; recognise omitted-variable bias and estimable combinations in rank-deficient cases.
targets.exitCheck: Find a coefficient variance or residual degree of freedom, and explain what fails when columns are linearly dependent.
steps: Derive a coefficient covariance or omitted-variable bias.
Identify an estimable linear combination when separate coefficients are not identifiable.

targets.title: Inference in regression
targets.exactScope: Under a normal linear model, distinguish individual t tests, nested-model F tests, mean-response intervals and prediction intervals.
targets.exitCheck: Derive a stated contrast test or nested-model comparison and explain why prediction has extra uncertainty.
steps: Derive a t contrast or nested-model F test under normal errors.
Construct mean-response and prediction intervals and explain their difference.

targets.title: SRS with and without replacement
targets.exactScope: Derive sample-mean/total expectation and variance; define the population variance convention and finite-population correction.
targets.exitCheck: Compare SRSWR and SRSWOR precision using the same convention and check the census limit n=N.
steps: Derive SRSWR/SRSWOR mean and total variances under one population convention.
Verify a proposed sampling algorithm assigns the right probability to every possible subset.

targets.title: Stratified means and allocation
targets.exactScope: Weight stratum estimates by population shares and compute variance under independent within-stratum SRS. Derive proportional and Neyman allocation with feasible bounds; include the short unequal-cost extension using n_h proportional to N_h S_h/sqrt(c_h) when its cost model applies.
targets.exitCheck: Find a stratified total and its variance, then minimise variance for fixed total sample size under stated equal costs.
steps: Calculate a stratified estimate and its sampling variance.
Derive an allocation under fixed size or stated costs, then check feasibility.

targets.title: Inclusion probabilities and unbiasedness
targets.exactScope: Use inclusion indicators, unequal inclusion probabilities and overlap of sample sets; distinguish a household count from a mean.
targets.exitCheck: Derive inclusion probabilities in an overlapping-frame design and prove inverse-probability weighting is unbiased.
steps: Compute one- and two-unit inclusion probabilities in a concrete design.
Prove an inverse-inclusion-weighted estimate is unbiased.

targets.title: CRD and one-way ANOVA
targets.exactScope: Specify treatment/error model, randomisation, independent normal equal-variance errors for exact F inference; decompose total SS.
targets.exitCheck: Build and justify a one-way ANOVA table, degrees of freedom and one estimable treatment contrast.
steps: Specify a CRD model and derive its sum-of-squares decomposition.
Construct the exact F test and one treatment contrast with valid error assumptions.

targets.title: Randomized blocks
targets.exactScope: Separate treatment from a blocking nuisance factor; state the additive model and randomisation within blocks.
targets.exitCheck: Construct the RBD sums of squares/degrees of freedom and explain what unmodelled treatment–block interaction would compromise.
steps: Justify randomisation within blocks and the additive model.
Build the RBD ANOVA and identify the interaction/error limitation.

targets.title: Latin square design
targets.exactScope: Use two blocking factors, one appearance of each treatment per row/column, valid randomisation and an additive model. Derive residual df=(p-1)(p-2). The ordinary residual-MSE treatment F test requires positive residual df, so a valid 2-by-2 Latin square has no such test even though the combinatorial design itself exists.
targets.exitCheck: Propose a valid Latin square, construct its ANOVA degrees of freedom, form the standard treatment F test only when p≥3 under the stated model, and diagnose p=2 as having zero residual df.
steps: Construct a valid Latin square and state its randomisation/model.
Derive its degrees of freedom and compare treatments with the right error term.

targets.title: Factorial main effects and interactions
targets.exactScope: Define main-effect and interaction contrasts in 2^k or simple mixed-level factorial designs. Declare the model and effect scaling, count degrees of freedom, and distinguish replication from pooling assumed-negligible interactions as error.
targets.exitCheck: Fill a partially specified factorial ANOVA table and identify when an interaction cannot be separated from error.
steps: Construct factorial main-effect and interaction contrasts.
Complete an ANOVA table and explain which error/interaction assumptions supply its degrees of freedom.

card.title: Compare domains before and after one cancellation.
card.focus: Cancellation as an equality on the original legal domain, not permission to silently restore excluded inputs.
card.purpose: Build the habit that every algebraic rewrite carries its domain with it, so later limits, likelihood supports and transformations do not inherit a false function equality.
card.centralCapability: Given a rational expression with a cancellable factor, identify the original domain, simplify algebraically, preserve every excluded point, and decide whether the original and simplified displays define the same function or only agree on their common domain.
card.principalObstacle: Cancellation makes the formulas look identical after simplification, which tempts the learner to forget that division by zero was illegal before the cancellation and that the removed point is still absent from the original function.
entryPrerequisites: Meaning of a real-valued function domain
No new T25 v4 session is required; prior F1 evidence may be used diagnostically
requiredOwnership: Find denominator-zero exclusions before simplifying.
Factor numerator and denominator without changing the stated domain.
Cancel a common nonzero factor while explicitly carrying the original exclusion.
Distinguish pointwise agreement on a shared domain from equality of functions with different domains.
State the equality set and domain of each displayed expression without plugging an excluded point into the original formula.
card.applicationScope: One-variable rational expressions and simple algebraic identities where a common factor can be cancelled and a removable-looking hole may be created by the original formula.
card.transferScope: A fresh expression with a parameter fixed in advance, multiple factors, or a disguised common factor where the same domain-preservation logic must be reconstructed rather than copied from a memorised example.
outOfScope: Principal-root and logarithm laws reserved for F1.2
General equation-solving transformations reserved for F2
Limit values and removable discontinuities reserved for C1
Changed-input function domains reserved for F3
card.exitCondition: On a fresh cancellable rational expression, state the original domain before any algebra, produce the simplified formula with the exclusion still attached, and correctly answer whether the two displayed formulas define the same function. Then repeat the domain comparison on a second unfamiliar cancellation without a hint.
card.nextArcBoundary: 002 · F1.2 moves from cancellation to principal-root, rational-power and logarithm hypotheses; it may use the domain-preservation habit established here but must not reopen cancellation as the main task.

sessions.lesson: A formula and its domain jointly specify a function. A rewrite is justified at legal inputs; it cannot enlarge the original domain.
sessions.evidenceWarning: Map each required-ownership item to actual independent evidence. These two tasks do not automatically discharge every obligation. Compile a bounded fresh probe for any unobserved claim.

card.title: Justify principal-root, rational-power and log-law conditions on a new expression.
card.focus: The sign and domain hypotheses hidden inside roots, rational powers and real logarithm identities.
card.purpose: Prevent familiar-looking identities from being applied outside the real domain or with the wrong principal-value convention, especially the recurrent mistake sqrt(u²)=u for negative u.
card.centralCapability: State and justify the real-domain conditions under which principal square-root, reduced rational-power and logarithm rewrites are valid, including the absolute-value consequence sqrt(u²)=|u| and positivity requirements for real log laws.
card.principalObstacle: Symbolic identities are often remembered without their hypotheses, so a learner may replace sqrt(u²) by u, use an unreduced rational exponent ambiguously, or split/combine logarithms when one of the required positive arguments is absent.
entryPrerequisites: F1.1 domain-preservation habit or equivalent established evidence
requiredOwnership: Explain why the principal square root is always nonnegative.
Replace sqrt(u²) by |u| and resolve |u| into sign cases when needed.
Determine the real domain of an even root, reciprocal root and reduced rational power.
State positivity conditions required for real logarithms and standard product/quotient/power laws.
Reject or qualify a proposed root, power or logarithm identity by giving the missing domain/sign condition.
card.applicationScope: Elementary real expressions involving square roots, nth roots, rational exponents and logarithms, with emphasis on exact legal domains rather than complex branches.
card.transferScope: A mixed expression combining a root or rational power with a logarithm where several restrictions interact and the learner must determine which rewrite is legal on which subset.
outOfScope: Solving radical/logarithmic equations as a full F2 task
Differentiation of roots/logs reserved for C3
card.exitCondition: For a fresh mixed root/power/log expression, state its real domain, justify or reject each requested identity with the exact sign/positivity condition, and correctly handle sqrt(u²) for both signs of u. A second changed-surface identity must be classified without prompting.
card.nextArcBoundary: 003 · F2.1 changes the question from legal expression rewrites to whether successive equation transformations preserve exactly the same solution set.

sessions.lesson: Principal roots are nonnegative. For reduced p/q with q>0, an even q requires nonnegative base; a negative exponent also excludes zero. Real logarithms require positive arguments.
sessions.evidenceWarning: Map each required-ownership item to actual independent evidence. These two tasks do not automatically discharge every obligation. Compile a bounded fresh probe for any unobserved claim.

card.title: Classify each step of one equation as equivalent or implication-only.
card.focus: Equations as claims about solution sets, with every algebraic step labelled by whether it is reversible under the stated conditions.
card.purpose: Replace the habit of treating every familiar manipulation as an equivalence with a proof-level check of reversibility, so extraneous candidates and lost solutions are detected at the step that creates them.
card.centralCapability: Given a chain of elementary equation transformations, determine for each step whether it is logically equivalent, only forward-implicative, or conditionally equivalent after a nonzero/sign/domain condition is stated.
card.principalObstacle: Operations such as squaring, multiplying by an expression that might be zero, dividing by a variable expression, or applying a non-injective function can change the solution set even though the algebra looks routine.
entryPrerequisites: F1 domain restrictions or equivalent established evidence
Elementary implication language from ordinary mathematics
requiredOwnership: Interpret solving an equation as finding exactly the inputs that make the original statement true.
Recognise obviously reversible addition, subtraction and multiplication by a known nonzero constant.
Detect when squaring or another non-injective operation can introduce extra candidates.
Detect when division or cancellation by an expression can discard a zero case unless it is separated first.
Check final candidates in the original equation whenever a step was implication-only.
card.applicationScope: Elementary real equations involving fractions, roots, squares, products and variable factors where the main task is logical classification of the transformation chain, not speed-solving a large equation family.
card.transferScope: A deliberately plausible worked solution containing one hidden non-equivalence; the learner must locate the first unsafe step, state its missing condition, and repair the argument without being told the error type.
outOfScope: Full rational-inequality sign charts reserved for F2.2
Advanced proof quantifiers reserved for F4
Calculus-based root counts reserved for C4
card.exitCondition: Audit a fresh multi-step equation solution by labelling every transformation equivalent, implication-only, or conditionally equivalent; identify any candidates that require checking and verify them against the original equation. Then diagnose one unfamiliar fake solution without a hint.
card.nextArcBoundary: 004 · F2.2 uses this solution-set discipline in inequalities, where multiplying/dividing by sign-unknown expressions and boundary handling become the main obstacle.

sessions.lesson: An equivalent step preserves the entire solution set. Squaring can introduce candidates; dividing by an expression can lose its zero cases.
sessions.evidenceWarning: Map each required-ownership item to actual independent evidence. These two tasks do not automatically discharge every obligation. Compile a bounded fresh probe for any unobserved claim.

card.title: Solve one inequality by sign cases and check all boundary points.
card.focus: Exact solution sets for rational or factored inequalities through critical points, sign intervals and boundary legality.
card.purpose: Make inequality solving structural rather than rule-memorisation: every zero, pole and sign change must be accounted for, and equality endpoints must be admitted or excluded for a stated reason.
card.centralCapability: Solve an elementary rational or factored real inequality by reducing it to sign analysis, listing numerator zeros and denominator exclusions, testing intervals, and assembling the exact final set with correct endpoint inclusion.
card.principalObstacle: Learners often cross-multiply through an expression of unknown sign, forget denominator poles, or treat all critical points alike even though zeros may be included under ≤/≥ while poles can never be included.
entryPrerequisites: F2.1 equivalence/implication discipline or equivalent evidence
Ordering and interval notation on the real line
requiredOwnership: Move all terms to one side without changing the inequality relation incorrectly.
Factor the relevant numerator and denominator far enough to expose critical points.
Separate zeros from excluded denominator points before interval testing.
Determine the sign on each interval by a justified test point or factor-parity argument.
Assemble the final union of intervals with endpoint inclusion matching both the inequality symbol and the original domain.
card.applicationScope: Polynomial-product and rational inequalities in one real variable with finitely many critical points and factorable structure suitable for exact sign analysis.
card.transferScope: A fresh inequality with repeated factors, a cancelled-looking factor, or a parameter fixed numerically so that the learner must decide which critical points actually change sign and which remain excluded.
outOfScope: Derivative-based monotonicity/root counts reserved for C4
card.exitCondition: Solve one unfamiliar rational inequality from the original expression to an exact interval-union answer, explicitly marking every zero and pole and justifying each boundary. Then explain why direct cross-multiplication would or would not have been legal in that example.
card.nextArcBoundary: 005 · F3.1 leaves equation/inequality solution sets and turns to functions evaluated at changed inputs, especially pulling a known domain back through the input transformation.

sessions.lesson: A rational sign analysis distinguishes numerator zeros from denominator exclusions. An even-multiplicity factor need not change sign.
sessions.evidenceWarning: Map each required-ownership item to actual independent evidence. These two tasks do not automatically discharge every obligation. Compile a bounded fresh probe for any unobserved claim.

card.title: Track one changed input and its legal domain.
card.focus: Treating the entire argument of a function as the input object and pulling the original domain back through a fixed change of input.
card.purpose: Eliminate substitution errors such as confusing f(x+h) with f(x)+h and establish the domain-preimage reasoning later required by composition, transformations, differentiation and likelihood support.
card.centralCapability: Given a function by formula and domain together with a fixed changed input such as x+h or ax+b, substitute the whole input correctly and determine exactly which x-values make the changed input land inside the original domain.
card.principalObstacle: A function rule is often manipulated as if x were a label rather than a slot, leading to partial substitution, output shifts in place of input shifts, or reuse of the old domain without solving the new membership condition.
entryPrerequisites: F2 solution-set reasoning for the resulting domain condition
requiredOwnership: Treat the displayed variable in f(x) as a placeholder for the entire new input.
Distinguish f(x+h), f(x)+h and f(x+h)-f(x) symbolically and conceptually.
Substitute a fixed affine or otherwise simple input into the complete defining formula.
Translate the requirement new_input ∈ Dom(f) into a condition on x and solve it exactly.
Check the resulting changed-input domain against any denominator, root or logarithm restrictions already present in the formula.
card.applicationScope: Elementary one-variable functions with explicit domains and fixed changed inputs, including rational, root and logarithmic formulas where domain pullback is the main task.
card.transferScope: An unfamiliar nested-looking expression where the input transformation is disguised algebraically; the learner must identify the actual argument first and derive its legal x-set without a template.
inScope: Preimage of a stated domain under a fixed input map
Domain pullback for fixed affine changes
Combining pulled-back and intrinsic formula restrictions
outOfScope: Parameter-case analysis and affine iteration reserved for F3.2
General composition/periodicity constraints reserved for A5.3
card.exitCondition: For a fresh domain-restricted function and a fixed changed input, write the changed formula, derive the exact legal x-domain from first principles, and explain in one sentence why f(x+h) is not f(x)+h. Repeat on a second changed surface without a hint.
card.nextArcBoundary: 006 · F3.2 keeps changed-input reasoning but makes the parameter or affine iteration itself variable, requiring case analysis rather than a single fixed pullback.

sessions.lesson: In f(E), the entire expression E is supplied as input. Transport the input-domain condition through E; distinguish input from output and state which symbols vary.
sessions.evidenceWarning: Map each required-ownership item to actual independent evidence. These two tasks do not automatically discharge every obligation. Compile a bounded fresh probe for any unobserved claim.

card.title: Analyse one parameter or affine-iteration question.
card.focus: Separating the running variable from parameters and constants while tracking how an affine rule changes under composition or repeated application.
card.purpose: Extend fixed changed-input reasoning into parameter-sensitive problems where the legal domain, output formula or repeated affine action can change qualitatively with the parameter value.
card.centralCapability: Given a one-variable function containing a parameter, or a simple affine map f(x)=ax+b used once or repeatedly, identify which symbols are variables versus fixed parameters, compute the requested changed or iterated expression correctly, and split into parameter cases whenever algebraic legality or behaviour changes.
card.principalObstacle: The learner may unconsciously let a parameter vary during a calculation, confuse f(f(x)) with an algebraic square, divide by a parameter expression that could be zero, or state one formula across exceptional cases where the affine map changes type.
entryPrerequisites: 005 / F3.1 whole-input substitution and domain pullback
requiredOwnership: Label the running variable, fixed parameter and numerical constants before manipulating the expression.
Compute f(ax+b), f(f(x)) or a short affine iterate by substituting the entire input rather than symbol-by-symbol guessing.
Detect parameter values that make a denominator zero, collapse a coefficient, or otherwise invalidate a generic algebraic step.
Separate exceptional parameter cases before division or cancellation and state the resulting formula in each legal case.
Explain how changing the parameter alters the map or legal input set without treating the parameter as a second free variable in the same task.
card.applicationScope: Elementary parameterised functions and short affine-iteration problems in which the main work is symbolic role-tracking, legal case separation and correct repeated substitution rather than general dynamical-systems analysis.
card.transferScope: A fresh affine or domain-restricted parameter problem whose exceptional case is hidden inside a coefficient or denominator, requiring the learner to discover the case split and recompute the expression rather than merely substitute a memorised formula.
outOfScope: General composition and periodicity theory reserved for A5.3
Injectivity, surjectivity and inverse construction reserved for F5.3
Calculus-based parameter optimisation or root counting
card.exitCondition: On one unfamiliar parameterised function or affine-iteration problem, identify all symbol roles, derive the requested expression from whole-input substitution, isolate every exceptional parameter value before any unsafe division, and give the correct casewise conclusion without a hint.
card.nextArcBoundary: 007 · F4.1 leaves function manipulation and begins explicit mathematical-claim logic: quantified negation, necessary/sufficient language and converse testing become the central task.

sessions.lesson: An affine iterate is composition, not a power of the output. Separate exceptional multipliers before using a geometric-sum formula.
sessions.evidenceWarning: Map each required-ownership item to actual independent evidence. These two tasks do not automatically discharge every obligation. Compile a bounded fresh probe for any unobserved claim.

card.title: Negate one quantified claim and test a converse.
card.focus: Reading the logical skeleton of a mathematical sentence before deciding whether the claim, its converse or its negation is true.
card.purpose: Build the minimum proof-language discipline needed throughout M.Stat questions: universal claims require universal support, existential claims require a witness, and negation must reverse the quantifier rather than merely insert the word not.
card.centralCapability: Translate an elementary mathematical claim into its quantifier-and-implication structure, negate it correctly, distinguish a statement from its converse and contrapositive, and classify necessary versus sufficient conditions using a concrete example or counterexample when appropriate.
card.principalObstacle: Natural language makes logically different claims sound similar, so learners often negate 'for every' as 'for every not', reverse an implication without justification, or confuse a condition that is sufficient with one that is necessary.
entryPrerequisites: Basic set/function notation from ordinary mathematics
Ability to evaluate a concrete candidate example
requiredOwnership: Negate a statement of the form 'for every x, P(x)' as an existential failure and negate an existential claim as a universal failure.
Distinguish P implies Q from the converse Q implies P and from the contrapositive not-Q implies not-P.
Translate 'P is sufficient for Q' and 'Q is necessary for P' into the same implication direction.
Test a proposed converse with a strategically chosen example rather than assuming symmetry of implication.
State exactly what would count as evidence for a universal claim, an existential claim and the negation of each.
card.applicationScope: Short algebraic, set-theoretic or function claims with one or two quantifiers and elementary implications, where the main task is logical translation and classification rather than a long proof.
card.transferScope: An unfamiliar verbal claim whose surface wording hides the quantifier order or implication direction; the learner must rewrite it symbolically enough to negate it and decide whether the converse survives.
inScope: Witnesses and counterexamples for claim testing
outOfScope: Writing a complete proof reserved for F4.2
Formal predicate-logic systems or truth-table courses
Measure-theoretic almost-sure quantifiers or advanced analysis logic
card.exitCondition: Given a fresh quantified implication, write its correct negation in words or symbols, state the converse and contrapositive, identify the necessary/sufficient relationship, and either validate or destroy the converse with a decisive elementary example without prompting.
card.nextArcBoundary: 008 · F4.2 turns this claim-reading skill into a finished mathematical argument: either a short proof under stated assumptions or a counterexample that decisively refutes the claim.

sessions.lesson: Negation swaps universal/existential quantifiers and negates the predicate. A converse reverses implication; it needs its own proof.
sessions.evidenceWarning: Map each required-ownership item to actual independent evidence. These two tasks do not automatically discharge every obligation. Compile a bounded fresh probe for any unobserved claim.

card.title: Write one short proof or a decisive counterexample.
card.focus: Closing a small mathematical claim with a complete chain of justified steps, or refuting it with one example that satisfies the assumptions and violates the conclusion.
card.purpose: Prevent two opposite failure modes common in entrance work: treating several confirming examples as proof, and offering a counterexample that does not actually meet the claim's hypotheses.
card.centralCapability: For an elementary implication or universal claim, decide whether a short direct/contrapositive argument is available or whether the claim is false, then produce either a complete assumption-to-conclusion proof or a valid counterexample with every required hypothesis checked.
card.principalObstacle: A plausible pattern can feel proven after a few examples, while an attempted counterexample can be irrelevant because it violates a hidden assumption; conversely, a proof can smuggle in the desired conclusion or an unstated converse.
entryPrerequisites: 007 / F4.1 quantified negation and implication structure
requiredOwnership: State the assumptions being used before starting the argument.
Choose direct proof, contrapositive reasoning or counterexample according to the actual logical form instead of stylistic preference.
Justify each algebraic or set-theoretic implication without assuming the conclusion or its converse.
For a counterexample, verify every hypothesis and then show explicitly which required conclusion fails.
Explain why multiple supporting examples cannot establish a universal claim but one valid counterexample can refute it.
card.applicationScope: Compact proofs and counterexamples built from elementary algebra, inequalities, sets, functions or finite structures, typically a few logically complete steps rather than theorem-heavy exposition.
card.transferScope: A fresh true-or-false claim with misleading numerical examples, where the learner must determine whether to prove or refute it and then produce a self-contained argument without being told the method.
outOfScope: Long theorem proofs requiring later subject machinery
Proofs using advanced real analysis or measure theory
card.exitCondition: Resolve one unfamiliar elementary claim completely: if true, give a short proof whose assumptions and implication steps are explicit; if false, give one counterexample that satisfies every premise and violates the conclusion. Then explain why the chosen argument is logically decisive.
card.nextArcBoundary: 009 · F5.1 moves from general claim logic to set membership as a calculational language for unions, intersections, complements, Cartesian products, images and preimages.

sessions.lesson: A proof must cover every allowed input. One verified admissible counterexample disproves a universal claim; several successful examples do not prove it.
sessions.evidenceWarning: Map each required-ownership item to actual independent evidence. These two tasks do not automatically discharge every obligation. Compile a bounded fresh probe for any unobserved claim.

card.title: Translate set operations and images/preimages by membership.
card.focus: Reducing set expressions and function-set statements to precise element-membership conditions rather than manipulating set symbols by visual pattern alone.
card.purpose: Create a reusable membership language for later probability events, supports, inverse images and equivalence classes, while keeping image/preimage notation distinct from inverse-function notation.
card.centralCapability: Given finite or rule-defined sets and an elementary function, translate unions, intersections, complements, set differences, Cartesian products, images and preimages into elementwise membership statements and use those statements to prove or refute a small set equality.
card.principalObstacle: Set notation encourages symbol pushing: learners may confuse element membership with subset inclusion, reverse the direction of images and preimages, or treat f^{-1}(B) as requiring an inverse function rather than as a preimage set.
entryPrerequisites: F3 function evaluation and changed-input notation
requiredOwnership: Distinguish x∈A from A⊆B and translate each relation into the correct verbal claim.
Expand membership in union, intersection, complement and difference using and/or/not conditions.
Interpret an ordered pair in A×B with the correct first-coordinate and second-coordinate membership requirements.
Compute f(A) as an image and f^{-1}(B) as a preimage without assuming that f is invertible.
Prove a small set identity by two-way membership or refute it by one element lying in exactly one side.
card.applicationScope: Finite sets, interval/rule-defined subsets of the reals and elementary functions where set operations, Cartesian products, images or preimages can be determined exactly from membership conditions.
card.transferScope: An unfamiliar nested set expression or preimage identity in which the notation is deliberately dense; the learner must unpack membership step by step and detect whether the claimed equality really holds.
outOfScope: Testing relation axioms reserved for F5.2
Injectivity, surjectivity and inverse-function construction reserved for F5.3
Probability calculations on events reserved for P3
card.exitCondition: For a fresh function and several stated sets, compute one image and one preimage, translate a nested set expression into membership logic, and prove or disprove one set equality elementwise without confusing preimage notation with an inverse function.
card.nextArcBoundary: 010 · F5.2 uses Cartesian-product and membership language to treat a relation as a set of ordered pairs and asks whether it is an equivalence relation and what its classes are.

sessions.lesson: Prove a set identity by tracking membership. Preimages preserve intersections; images can merge distinct source points.
sessions.evidenceWarning: Map each required-ownership item to actual independent evidence. These two tasks do not automatically discharge every obligation. Compile a bounded fresh probe for any unobserved claim.

card.title: Check a relation and list its equivalence classes.
card.focus: Testing reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity from the actual ordered-pair rule, then turning a valid equivalence relation into disjoint equivalence classes.
card.purpose: Make relation questions proof-driven rather than pattern-driven and establish the partition viewpoint needed to reason cleanly about 'same-type' groupings on finite or elementary sets.
card.centralCapability: Given a relation on a stated set, interpret it as a subset of the Cartesian square, test reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity with explicit reasoning, decide whether it is an equivalence relation, and if so compute the equivalence classes and verify that they partition the underlying set.
card.principalObstacle: A relation can look symmetric or grouping-like in a few examples while failing one axiom elsewhere; transitivity in particular is often asserted from a diagram or intuition instead of checking the implication xRy and yRz implies xRz.
entryPrerequisites: 009 / F5.1 Cartesian products and membership logic
requiredOwnership: Read xRy as membership of (x,y) in a specified relation and keep the underlying set explicit.
Test reflexivity by checking every element is related to itself, or refute it with one missing diagonal case.
Test symmetry by reversing related ordered pairs and distinguish symmetry from merely having many reciprocal examples.
Test transitivity from two composable relation facts and produce a concrete violating triple when it fails.
For a valid equivalence relation, compute [x]={y:xRy}, identify duplicate classes and verify the distinct classes are disjoint and cover the set.
card.applicationScope: Finite sets and elementary relations defined by equality-like rules such as congruence, parity, shared attributes or simple algebraic conditions where the three equivalence axioms can be checked directly.
card.transferScope: A fresh relation presented as a formula, table or pair list where one axiom is subtly violated or where several named elements represent the same equivalence class, requiring proof rather than visual grouping.
outOfScope: Injective/surjective function tests reserved for F5.3
General partial orders or order theory
Quotient vector spaces or quotient groups
Probability conditional equivalence or statistical sufficiency
card.exitCondition: On an unfamiliar finite or elementary relation, decide each of reflexive, symmetric and transitive with a proof or explicit counterexample; if all hold, list every distinct equivalence class and verify that the classes cover the set without overlap.
card.nextArcBoundary: 011 · F5.3 keeps the stated-domain discipline but switches from arbitrary relations to functions: injectivity, surjectivity and construction of an inverse on the declared domain/codomain become the sole focus.

sessions.lesson: An equivalence relation needs reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity on the declared set. Its equivalence classes partition that set.
sessions.evidenceWarning: Map each required-ownership item to actual independent evidence. These two tasks do not automatically discharge every obligation. Compile a bounded fresh probe for any unobserved claim.

card.title: Test injectivity/surjectivity and construct an inverse on stated sets.
card.focus: Treating domain and codomain as part of a function's definition, then testing one-to-one and onto claims against those stated sets before attempting to invert the rule.
card.purpose: Close the foundation function block with the exact condition under which an inverse function exists, while preventing algebraic inverse-formula manipulations from replacing proofs of injectivity and surjectivity.
card.centralCapability: Given a function together with an explicit domain and codomain, decide injectivity and surjectivity from their definitions, identify whether the function is bijective, and construct and verify an inverse exactly on the sets where a two-sided inverse is legitimate.
card.principalObstacle: A familiar formula can tempt the learner to announce an inverse without checking the declared domain/codomain, to confuse solving y=f(x) with proving bijectivity, or to call a function noninvertible globally when an explicitly stated restriction would make the requested map bijective.
entryPrerequisites: 009 / F5.1 images, preimages and membership logic
007-008 / F4 quantified claims and proof/counterexample discipline
requiredOwnership: State the domain and codomain before judging injectivity or surjectivity; recognise that changing either can change the answer.
Test injectivity from f(x1)=f(x2) implying x1=x2, or refute it with two distinct legal inputs sharing one output.
Test surjectivity by taking an arbitrary codomain element and determining whether at least one legal preimage exists, rather than merely inspecting several outputs.
Conclude that an inverse function on the stated codomain exists exactly when the map is bijective, and distinguish this from the always-defined preimage-set notation f^{-1}(B).
Construct the inverse rule where legitimate and verify both compositions on their proper domains, including any endpoint or branch restriction required by the stated sets.
card.applicationScope: Elementary real-valued, finite-set and parameter-light functions with explicitly stated domains/codomains where injectivity, surjectivity, bijectivity and inverse construction can be settled directly from definitions and algebra.
card.transferScope: A fresh function whose algebraic inverse formula looks plausible but whose domain or codomain hides a failure of injectivity or surjectivity, requiring the learner to diagnose the set-level obstruction and state the smallest valid conclusion.
inScope: Two-sided inverse verification and simple domain restriction
outOfScope: General composition/periodicity constraints reserved for A5.3
Linear-map invertibility and matrix inverse reserved for M3
card.exitCondition: For one unfamiliar function with explicitly stated domain and codomain, prove or refute injectivity and surjectivity separately, decide bijectivity, and if bijective construct an inverse and verify both compositions on the correct sets without hints.
card.nextArcBoundary: 012 · A1.1 leaves foundational set/function logic and begins polynomial structure: factor/remainder reasoning and Vieta relations become the central tools for connecting roots with coefficients.

sessions.lesson: Injectivity compares inputs; surjectivity depends on the codomain. An inverse as a two-sided map exists exactly for a bijection.
sessions.evidenceWarning: Map each required-ownership item to actual independent evidence. These two tasks do not automatically discharge every obligation. Compile a bounded fresh probe for any unobserved claim.

card.title: Use factor/remainder and Vieta in one root-coefficient problem.
card.focus: Moving fluently between polynomial values, linear factors, roots and coefficient relations without expanding or solving more of the polynomial than the question requires.
card.purpose: Build the compact polynomial toolkit repeatedly useful in entrance algebra: the factor/remainder theorem identifies roots and divisibility, while Vieta converts symmetric information about roots into coefficient constraints.
